wake.description: a scheduled time to come back to something
wake.$comment: A wake carries no patch to apply when it fires: a rule's produce already writes the entity it matched. Patching a wake's target declaratively would need a rule that names that target.

at.description: when it is next due; absent once a one-shot has fired, or once a recurrence has ended

target.description: what the wake is about; when absent, the entity carrying it

note.description: a line for whoever is woken: why the wake was set

every.description: how it recurs: a duration (30m, 2h, 1d), five cron fields (0 9 * * 1-5), or @hourly/@daily/@weekly/@monthly; a cron line may end with an IANA time zone (0 9 * * 1-5 America/New_York), otherwise UTC

while.description: how it recurs while something holds: {match, every} in order, a query over the whole store and the cadence it asks for; at each firing the first whose query finds anything sets the next instant, else every does, and with neither the wake sleeps until a write makes one hold

match.description: holds while this query finds anything

every.description: the cadence while it holds, written as wake.every is

wake_new.title: Schedule a wake
wake_new.description: Come back to something later: once at an instant, or on a cadence. Each firing knocks whoever attends the target with the note: a persona's operator, or the session opened on a topic (a goal or project that is its own topic). Returns the wake.

target.description: What the wake is about: a persona, a topic, a goal or project id.

every.description: How it recurs: a duration (30m, 1d), five cron fields with an optional time zone (0 7 * * * America/Detroit), or @hourly/@daily/@weekly/@monthly.

at.description: When it is next due; with every, the first firing. Without every, it fires once.

note.description: A line for whoever is woken: what to do.
